I will keep my land in the usual Quzhou double-cropping pattern: winter wheat followed by summer maize. I am making that choice because this is the crop system I know best, it is the main local system in Quzhou County, and it matches our weather: the wheat season is dry and needs a few irrigations, while most of our rain comes in the maize season. I am 69, so I will not take on vegetables or other labor-heavy crops that need more hand work, more frequent spraying, and more marketing risk. I want a steady grain harvest, simpler field work, and lower water pressure. Based on Quzhou and North China Plain research, I am inferring a moderate-input plan rather than the very high fertilizer and irrigation levels many farmers used in the past, because water is limited and lower-to-moderate rates can still hold yield well in this rotation. Sources I used: [PMC Quzhou site description](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5290742/), [2024 irrigation study for North China Plain wheat-maize rotation](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378377424000611), [2022 long-term irrigation study](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378429021003105), [2019 nitrogen assessment for North China Plain](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6920463/), [2023 water-fertilizer-saving study](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S037837742200600X).
